correctness.rationale: For each k>=1, use Kleiner’s fixed-mean reduction to shifted binomials and established unique zero at sharp threshold μ_k for parameters (ℓ,r)=(0,k+d_k). Every other finite rival at μ_k is negative. For each of finitely many ℓ in [0,k], letting r→∞ gives the Poisson difference with λ=s+Δ_k, s=k−ℓ, Δ_k∈(0,1), and λ²/((s+1)(s+2))<1, hence each limit is strictly negative. Uniform binomial-to-Poisson TV bound O(λ²/r) on compact μ-neighborhood plus continuity of finitely many remaining rivals yields one uniform gap and an open two-sided region with the same global optimum. Differentiation of the two equal binomial masses gives slope 2c/[m q(1−q)]. Independently checked seven k crossing/rival grids to trial cap400, not an exhaustive proof of unbounded trial lengths.

value.rationale: A globally sharp signed excess—not just the sign threshold—among arbitrary-length Poisson-binomial sums provides meaningful sensitivity and robustness at a sharp reversal boundary. Uniform control over infinitely many allowable trial counts is not routine pointwise continuity, and the first derivative can be used to analyze perturbations of the constrained extremum.
